{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Clan MacAlister is a Scottish Clan and a branch of Clan Donald.","title":"Clan MacAlister"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The clan is the earliest branch to have split off from Clan Donald, claiming descent from Alasdair Mòr, son of Domhnall founder of Clan Donald.","title":"Clan MacAlister"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" From Alasdair Mòr the clans takes its surname \"MacAlister\"; this surname is an Anglicisation of the Gaelic \"MacAlasdair\" meaning \"son of Alasdair\".","title":"Clan MacAlister"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" In the 15th century the chief of the clan was seated in Kintyre, and the clan was centred there until the 18th century, when a chief sold the family estate in preference to a lowland estate.","title":"Clan MacAlister"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Clan MacAlister of Antrim is an Irish clan and a branch of Clan MacAlister of Scotland.","title":"Clan MacAlister of Antrim"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The clan was established as an Irish sept in Antrim in north-east Ulster, as gallóglaigh (galloglasses), in the service of the Lord of the Isles and Clan MacDonald of Dunnyveg.","title":"Clan MacAlister of Antrim"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"The seat of Alexanders of Menstrite, a sept of Clan MacAlister of Scotland, is at a castle in Clackmannanshire, that was at one time owned by a family who were created Baronets of Menstire in what year?"}
